stem.en: A jar holds 10 g of salt in 90 g of water. You add 10 g more water. Which working gives the mass by mass percentage now?

text.en: (10 g / 100 g) × 100, because the salt did not change
(10 g / 100 g of water) × 100, because there is now 100 g of water
(10 g / 90 g) × 100, because 90 g was the first amount of water

explanation.en: The solution is now 10 g of salt plus 100 g of water, which is 110 g. So the working is (10 g / 110 g) × 100 = 9.1 %. Option b is the common mistake: it does not use the whole solution, only the water. Option d does the same with the old amount of water. Option a uses the solution as it was before you added water.

hints.en: Write down everything in the jar now, and add it up.
Does the bottom of the fraction hold the water, or everything?
